note: Obliger centrally means oblige/require/compel/force. 'To help/aid' is an older politeness/favor sense, and 'have to' is usually expressed through être obligé de rather than bare obliger.
proposed_english: to oblige; to require; to compel; to force; to do a favor for (older/polite use); to have to (être obligé de)
to notice; to observe; to remark/state

note: Charger has core everyday meanings load and charge (including a battery/device), which are missing or narrowed to a firearm. It can also entrust/assign in constructions.
proposed_english: to load; to charge; to charge a battery/device; to load a firearm; to entrust/assign; to overact (context-dependent)

note: Or is both the noun gold and the conjunction/discourse connector 'now/yet/however/whereas'. Conjunction POS is listed but no conjunction meaning is provided.
proposed_english: gold; now; yet; however; whereas (formal/written connector)

note: Blague simply means joke/prank; 'sly joke' is unnecessarily narrow.
Étrange means strange/odd/unusual. 'Foreign' is not the normal modern learner meaning; that is étranger/étrangère.
Dépêcher means dispatch/send, but its overwhelmingly common learner use is se dépêcher = hurry. That reflexive construction is missing.
proposed_english: to dispatch; to send; to hurry (se dépêcher)

note: Chaud means hot as well as warm; omitting 'hot' is a basic learner error.
Parole centrally means speech/word and also one's word/promise; in the plural paroles means words/lyrics. The current 'swear to God!' gloss is not an appropriate core definition.
proposed_english: word; speech; one's word/promise; right to speak; words/lyrics (plural)

note: Parier means bet/wager. The 'mate/couple' sense is obsolete/rare and should not lead a modern learner entry.
Plusieurs functions both as an indefinite determiner and independently as a pronoun ('several [of them]'). Adjective-only POS is incomplete.
The surname is irrelevant. But means goal/aim/objective/purpose and, in sports, a goal; those core meanings should be cleanly presented.
Signe is the noun sign/gesture/indication, but the same common spelling is also a finite/imperative form of signer ('signs; sign!').
proposed_english: sign; gesture; indication; signs; sign! (forms of signer, context-dependent)
proposed_pos: noun / finite verb form / imperative form

note: 'Draft constitution' is an overly specific dictionary artifact. Projet should teach project/plan/proposal/draft.
Libérer means release and also free/liberate; the current one-word gloss is unnecessarily narrow.
proposed_english: to free; to release; to liberate

note: Pute is vulgar/offensive. It means prostitute/whore and is also used as an insult or intensifier; register must be explicit rather than presenting misogynistic English slurs as neutral synonyms.
proposed_english: prostitute; whore; insulting term for a woman; fucking (intensifier) — vulgar/offensive
